topic.title: Randomized Linear Algebra and Spectral Approximation
topic.area: Sparsity, Low-Rank Models, and Dimensionality Reduction
topic.overview: This topic develops efficient ways to estimate matrix structure, distances, and spectral quantities without processing every entry at full cost. Methods include random projections, low-rank approximation, streaming algorithms, and adaptive sensing. A representative approach uses kernel-density queries to accelerate operations on kernel matrices, with explicit error guarantees and computational lower bounds.
topic.whyItMatters: Many learning algorithms depend on large matrix operations that dominate memory or runtime. Structured access and approximation can make them feasible, but the savings depend on the required precision and on which information the access model actually provides.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives estimate singular vectors and study radial-basis representations. Later work analyzes kernel approximation, matrix streams, and randomized projections. Recent papers extend density-based matrix computation and adaptive eigenvector estimation, with related spectral analyses appearing in structured sequence models.
openQuestions: Which access models remain realistic once data-loading costs are included?
How can approximation guarantees predict downstream learning quality rather than matrix error alone?
